message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). For PRS-comparable performance, only PGS001784 reports a covariates-regressed-out PRS metric (Nagelkerke R2=0.014661), but it comes from a broad global-biobank framework paper and its headline AUROC=0.868 is a full-model metric with substantial covariate adjustment, so it is not strong standalone PRS evidence. PGS002054 is from a UKB portability framework and reports only partial-r=0.0144 (weak/modest and framework-derived). The disease-focused AAA study model PGS000753 (MVP/MAYO-VDB; Circulation) provides the clearest PRS-specific signal via an OR per SD of 1.37 (moderate effect size) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding the comparability issues of covariate-boosted full-model AUROC. However, confidence is limited because several newer disease-focused PRS-CS/shaPRS models (PGS003972/PGS003973/PGS003429) report only full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown or differing covariates and no PRS-only metrics/effect sizes, making direct cross-model ranking uncertain."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target alcohol dependence via alcohol use disorder / problematic alcohol use, with phenotype fields indicating AUD endpoints (DSM-5 criteria count for PGS000201/PGS000202; AUD diagnosis for PGS002738/PGS002739). Among them, PGS002738 is best supported by endpoint fidelity (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder), disease-focused multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB), and the strongest visible discriminative evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 [1.54–2.51]) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). However, confidence is not high because none of the candidates report PRS-comparable AUC or PRS-only R2, covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (limiting comparability), and PGS000201 reports only a small incremental ΔR2 (0.01192) on a related but not exact trait label (‘Problematic alcohol use’), making the overall evidence set incomplete for a clearly high-quality pick."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004913","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to alcoholic liver cirrhosis by trait_efo, with acceptable endpoint alignment in phenotyping_reported (PGS000704: “Alcoholic cirrhosis”; PGS001777: “Cirrhosis (males)”/alcohol related; PGS004913: “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis”). However, none reports clearly PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R² are null across the set), so full-model AUROC/C-index values are not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence. Among the candidates, PGS004913 is from a disease-focused study explicitly targeting alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers and reports a PRS-comparable R²=0.029 plus an OR (top vs bottom PRS deciles)=4.4, with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), making its performance evidence more directly interpretable than PGS000704’s covariate-including time-to-event C-index (0.711) and PGS001777’s unknown covariates and very small variant set (3 SNPs). Remaining limitation: evidence is still incomplete/heterogeneous (different study designs and metrics; PGS004913’s R² is modest and not explicitly stated as covariate-regressed-out), so the direct-match choice is supported but not high-certainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally coherent phenotyping (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001262 provides explicit PGS-only performance (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.01304) and a small incremental AUROC (0.0098), with endpoint fidelity via a direct doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype and only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Competing UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet models (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) are from the same framework publication; within that sibling set, PGS001262 has the strongest PRS-only R2 and AUROC and the highest full-model AUROC, making it the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. Main limitation: the strongest-looking discrimination values in the pool are mostly full-model C-index/AUROC from other studies (e.g., MVP benchmarking scores and the biomarker paper) without clearly PRS-only metrics, and several newer ICD10 I20 models report only ORs with unknown covariates; this makes cross-study ranking uncertain and prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002089","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. However, most are from framework-style UK Biobank sweeps (\"813 traits\" sparse snpnet; \"Portability of 245 polygenic scores\") or have limited/less comparable performance reporting. Among the EUR-focused options, PGS002089 (LDpred2, 22,026 variants; UKB-derived portability study) has the strongest available PRS-comparable metric in the context (partial correlation 0.0919 [0.0775–0.1063]) and a more genome-wide shrinkage approach than the very sparse snpnet models (10 variants) from the pan-trait framework paper. The main limitation is that the portability-study models do not report PRS-only AUROC/R² here (only partial-r), and the EAS-only Taiwanese models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298), making cross-candidate performance comparability and generalizability uncertain; therefore the direct-match recommendation is present but not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is explicitly aligned to the target disease (trait_reported/trait_efo: aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported: incident aortic stenosis cases), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (1,119,377), and provides a representative discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92) in a large European evaluation sample (n=446,895). The main limitation is that the reported C-index is a full-model metric with multiple clinical covariates (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, CAD, lipids, BMI, smoking, renal failure), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the incremental contribution of the PRS cannot be isolated; competing direct-match models (PGS005254/255/256) report HRs but lack comparable discrimination metrics, leaving some residual uncertainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the exact target trait are present (e.g., PGS001135 ‘Arthritis (nos)’ with trait_efo=arthritis; also PGS004477/PGS004547 ‘M13 (Other arthritis)’ with trait_efo=arthritis). Among these, PGS001135 has the clearest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported ‘Arthritis (nos)’) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus a European-selected validation record, enabling interpretation and a heritability sanity-check (PGS R2 well below the provided h2_liability=0.0610). However, the evidence remains limited for a strong recommendation because PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (‘Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits’), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation, and its PRS-only discrimination is modest. The alternative exact-EFO arthritis models (PGS004477/PGS004547) lack comparable performance metrics (only an OR without CI and unknown covariates), so they cannot be more strongly supported from the visible metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002727","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match asthma PRS candidates are present. PGS002727 is preferred because it is explicitly asthma-focused (\"Multiancestral polygenic risk score for pediatric asthma\"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 985,837 variants), and reports a comparatively strong effect size (OR=1.57 per SD, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) with AUROC=0.66, suggesting meaningful PRS signal. Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/framework or portability-style efforts (e.g., UKB 813-traits snpnet models; UKB portability/partial-correlation models) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models, or have weaker/less comparable evidence (e.g., very small validation sizes like PGS000037/PGS000799; incident-only packaging; or missing PRS-comparable metrics). Main limitation: PGS002727 targets pediatric asthma (endpoint restriction vs generic asthma) and lists covariates as unknown, so despite strong reported association and large evaluation sample size, endpoint generalizability and metric comparability remain uncertain, preventing a high-confidence/high-quality designation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are primarily evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (therapy-/context-specific rather than generic atopic eczema), and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (severity-restricted) with a small validation sample (n=676) and only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.93, R² 0.49) that are not PRS-only and are difficult to interpret against the heritability sanity-check. Among the remaining generic incident atopic dermatitis models, PGS002755 (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants) has strong phenotype alignment (incident atopic dermatitis), a genome-wide shrinkage method, EUR evaluation, and reports an HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (1.123–1.391) in a very large validation (n=337,910). PGS004587 is also incident AD but uses only 23 genome-wide significant SNPs and shows a weaker HR (1.153; 1.037–1.282), making it less supported structurally and empirically. Confidence is not high because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R², and the best-supported choice relies on effect-size evidence plus method/endpoint alignment rather than directly comparable PRS discrimination metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates are abundant for atrial fibrillation; the best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS005168 because it is phenotype-aligned (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both atrial fibrillation), comes from a disease-focused large multi-cohort AF meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many AF cohorts listed), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports strong validation discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663). Main limitation: the reported C-index is a full-model metric with covariates including CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), which domain guidance flags as risk-wrapper packaging that can inflate/obscure standalone PRS contribution; no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided here, so confidence is reduced despite strong overall study/endpoint evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct concept matches via trait_efo including atrial flutter, but only PGS001263 is specifically aligned to the target in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported (“Atrial flutter”), whereas the others use the broader combined endpoint “atrial fibrillation and flutter” (and PGS001339 is additionally time-to-event). PGS001263 also provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517) with basic covariates, and its PGS-only R2 is below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), supporting metric plausibility. However, confidence is limited because PGS001263 comes from a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework (the “813 traits” snpnet paper), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable externally than disease-focused scores, and the competing portability-study models (PGS001841/PGS002050) lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, preventing a clean performance-based comparison across study families."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (autism spectrum disorder) and are evaluated in European ancestry. PGS000327 has stronger endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is explicitly 'Autism spectrum disorder' vs PGS002790's 'Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)'), comes from an ASD-focused Nat Genet study, and provides supportive PRS signal evidence via an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) and higher reported full-model R² (0.0245 vs 0.00546). Main limitation: neither model reports clearly PRS-only (no-covariates) AUC/R², so performance comparability is limited and confidence cannot be high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 20 candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and strength of reported PRS signal. PGS000452 (Cancer PRSweb; GWAS Hits; 28 variants; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL) has phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and shows the strongest combined evidence among the listed models: relatively high full-model AUROC (0.632, 95% CI 0.616–0.647) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.663, 95% CI 1.57–1.761) and the largest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² in this set (0.0487), outperforming close siblings from the same publication family (e.g., PGS000454 AUROC 0.632 but slightly lower OR; PGS000456 AUROC 0.63). Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², so comparisons rely on full-model metrics and effect sizes (which may be partly covariate-influenced), and several near-clone PRSweb models are very close, keeping confidence below High."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002032","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO concept (bilirubin metabolism disease). PGS000924 targets a broader composite endpoint (\"Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism\") and is explicitly a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score (\"across 813 traits\"), which domain guidance flags as a common underperformer in external validation despite attractive internal metrics; its very high full-model AUROC is also not a substitute for PRS-only evidence. PGS001824 and PGS002032 both match the specific endpoint (\"Disorders of bilirubin excretion\"), come from the same portability framework paper, and report the same PRS-comparable metric (partial-r=0.0716 in EUR), making them the most endpoint-faithful options here. Between those two near-clones, PGS002032 is mildly preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 19,768 variants vs penalized regression with 22 variants) given identical phenotype, covariates, and reported partial-r. Limitation: the key PRS-comparable metrics (AUC/R²) are missing for both portability candidates and the evidence is confined to UK Biobank-derived evaluation, so overall support is not strong enough for a high-quality designation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches within the bipolar disorder spectrum (PGS002786: bipolar disorder; PGS002787: bipolar I; PGS002788: bipolar II), share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and similar genome-wide variant counts (~935k–949k), leaving limited structural basis to differentiate. For the target trait labeled broadly as “bipolar disorder,” PGS002786 has the closest trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo both bipolar disorder) and comparable evaluation context; however, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields describe non-diagnosis cognitive/behavioral measures rather than bipolar disorder case status, and the only reported metric is a small partial R² (~0.0025–0.0031) without PRS-only AUROC/AUC. Given this limited and potentially non-endpoint-faithful evidence, a clearly high-quality direct-match choice cannot be made from the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches at the broad concept level via coagulation-defect endpoints, but none is a clean, clearly best-supported PRS for the generic target “blood coagulation disease.” PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) and provides the most explicit PRS-comparable performance evidence (PGS-only AUROC/R² reported, with only basic covariates), but it is a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework score with an extremely low variant count (1) and a time-to-event phenotype (“TTE other coagulation defects”), both of which are warning signals for generalizability and endpoint fidelity. The two alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the broad blood coagulation disease umbrella) and lack AUROC/R², reporting only partial correlation; between them they are near-identical in endpoint/covariates/publication, with PGS002034 having a much larger variant set (LDpred2, 32,552 vs 45) but without additional performance evidence to clearly justify preferring the narrower congenital endpoint over the broader-mapped model. Given these tradeoffs and missing/heterogeneous evidence, a direct match exists but is not high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant; among those shown, PGS004153 is a direct breast cancer model (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer) with strong reported discrimination in European evaluation (AUROC=0.6625, R²=0.0764) and a large variant set (1,133,268) using a multi-PRS approach (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV), which is a positive structural signal per the provided domain guidance (multi-score aggregation tends to outperform single-score construction). Competing direct-match models include other strong UKB-based method-benchmark scores (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025 with AUROC≈0.6598 and R²≈0.0736–0.0739) and earlier disease-focused scores (e.g., PGS000332 AUROC=0.75 but full-model C-index with multiple non-genetic covariates; PGS000007 AUROC=0.78 but also full-model with age/sex), but these either have slightly weaker PRS-comparable metrics than PGS004153 (within the same 2023 multi-method family) or rely on full-model metrics that are not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Main limitation: the context provides no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² for PGS004153 (metrics appear as full-model), and several near-tied candidates from the same 2023 benchmarking family exist, so the preference is evidence-based but not unequivocal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000316","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease at the EFO level, but several have endpoint restrictions or framework-study penalties. PGS000316 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is not from a pan-trait/portability framework paper, and reports a high AUROC (0.879 with CI) in European validation; its development also spans multiple cohorts (B58C, UKBS), which is supportive versus UKB-only framework-derived scores. The main limitation is that the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), and covariates are listed as Unknown, so the degree of covariate contribution cannot be assessed; additionally, PGS000040 reports an even higher full-model AUROC (0.90) but with similarly unclear covariate comparability, leaving some residual uncertainty in ranking."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003428","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is preferred because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis study (Hum Mol Genet: “GWAS meta-analyses clarify genetics of cervical phenotypes and inform risk stratification for cervical cancer”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred; ~2.9M variants), which is structurally favorable versus sparse/hits-only scores and versus the pan-trait UKB framework snpnet model (PGS001299). However, the evidence is not strong enough for a high-quality designation because the available performance evidence is limited and largely full-model/time-to-event style (C-index 0.613; HR 1.33 with SE only) without clearly reported PRS-only discrimination, and competing EUR incident-cervical-cancer models (PGS000073/PGS000784) show higher full-model AUROC (~0.745) but with heavier covariate sets and small variant counts, making cross-model metric comparison non-decisive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004546","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis or a very close composite endpoint (cholelithiasis + cholecystitis). PGS004546 is preferred because it targets the exact ICD10-aligned endpoint (K80 cholelithiasis; trait_efo=cholelithiasis; phenotyping_reported=K80) and provides a PRS effect size (OR=1.2986 per SD), which is the strongest PRS-comparable signal available among the exact-cholelithiasis models in this context (stronger than PGS004476 OR=1.2194). Competing models either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks with weaker endpoint/study archetype signals despite having some metrics (PGS001174 is from the ‘813 traits’ sparse framework; PGS001861/PGS002072 are from a UKB portability sweep and report only partial-r), or are ancestry-specific to EAS evaluation (PGS005150), limiting general direct-use unless EAS is the intended population. Main limitation: key comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for PGS004546 and covariates are listed as unknown, so the evidence is insufficient to call a clearly high-quality winner over the better-metric-reported but framework-origin alternatives; hence sub-optimal with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match CKD models are present. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused (stage 3+; eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a dedicated CKD PRS paper (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”, Nat Med) with multi-ancestry evaluation and a reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65), indicating moderate PRS signal. However, the evidence is not fully decisive because the reported AUROC (0.78) appears to be a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, limiting comparability across candidates. Competing models either have weaker/less coherent phenotype alignment (e.g., PGS000728 uses eGFR as phenotype; PGS000859 is tied to a diabetes subtype), are framework-style (PGS001272), or provide only modest effect-size evidence without clearer PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS002757, PGS005113), so PGS002237 is preferred but with residual uncertainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match COPD candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001783 is preferred because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD) and comes from a large multi-biobank development context (many contributing cohorts listed) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto), which domain guidance treats as structurally stronger and typically more externally robust than sparse/pan-trait UKB framework scores. Its reported PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) is also consistent with the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability ~0.0388), supporting metric plausibility. Main limitation: evidence remains incomplete/heterogeneous across candidates—several alternatives are also direct matches (e.g., PGS001332/1333/1334 from a pan-trait UKB framework with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 but known generalizability concerns; PGS002062/001850 are portability-framework with only partial-r; PGS004466/004536 report only OR with unknown covariates). Additionally, PGS001783’s validation sample size is relatively small (n=7,128) and AUROC is reported only as a generic AUROC without an explicit PGS-only AUROC, lowering certainty versus an ideal, clearly PRS-only discrimination report."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (cirrhosis of liver), but several are explicitly alcohol-related subtypes (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) and one has phenotype wording that appears alcohol-related despite a generic label (PGS000776: phenotyping_reported references an at-risk NAFLD cohort and time-to-hospitalisation). Among the two cleanest generic cirrhosis endpoints (PGS000726 and PGS004621), PGS004621 is best supported by a disease-focused, recent Nat Genet study with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), very large evaluation sample size (n=1,153,995), and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), while reporting moderate discrimination (AUROC 0.68) and an OR effect size (1.42). However, confidence is limited because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², making performance comparisons across studies uncertain; several reported AUROCs are full-model metrics and thus not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the target EFO and sharing the same reported/phenotyped endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), same publication (UKB portability framework), similar ancestry evaluation (EUR primary; some SAS), and similarly weak reported PRS-comparable performance (partial-r ~0.056 in EUR; no AUC/R2/effect sizes shown). With endpoint fidelity and covariates essentially identical and performance indistinguishable, the main differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (32,552 vs 45), which is a moderate positive signal when other evidence is tied. However, because both models come from a portability/framework study and lack standard PRS-comparable metrics (AUC/R2) or effect sizes, the evidence is insufficient for a clearly strong recommendation, so the direct-match selection remains sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all = corneal dystrophy) and come from the same UKB portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size, so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiators visible are method/structure and the selected European validation metric: PGS002042 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (59,944 vs 38) and shows a higher partial correlation in the selected European validation record (0.0471 vs 0.0384), which together support it as the stronger sibling under the provided domain guidance. Confidence is moderate because neither model reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 or effect sizes, and both originate from a portability-style framework where external generalization beyond the shown context is uncertain."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003725","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are abundant (85). Among the visible candidates, PGS003725 is a strong direct match on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly “Coronary artery disease”), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (1,296,172), and comes from a disease-focused multi-ancestry CAD PRS study (Nat Med 2023) with multi-ancestry evaluation reported. It also reports strong per-SD effect sizes (HR 1.75; OR 2.14), which is supportive when PRS-only AUROC/R2 are not available. Limitation: across the candidate set, most reported AUROC/C-index values are full-model and covariate-dependent, and PGS003725 lacks explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics in the provided metadata, making it hard to conclusively rank it above other strong CAD candidates (e.g., other LDpred/PRS-CS/large-variant CAD scores) without more comparable PRS-only performance evidence; therefore confidence is moderate and the outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001331","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo=Crohn disease; phenotyping_reported indicates Crohn’s disease endpoints). PGS001330 is a time-to-event endpoint, which the provided domain guidance flags as a potential weakness for generic disease-risk deployment when comparable case-control endpoints exist. Between the two near-clone snpnet framework models from the same pan-trait UKB paper (PGS001330/PGS001331), PGS001331 has slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics in European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with similar covariates and validation size, making it the better-supported pick within that family. PGS004254 reports a much higher AUROC (0.72) and strong OR (2.18), but the context indicates this is a full-model AUROC with no PGS-only AUROC/R² reported, so per the domain guidance it is not directly comparable as PRS performance evidence; additionally, its publication focus (immune checkpoint inhibitor-mediated colitis) raises uncertainty about general-purpose Crohn’s disease risk deployment despite the phenotype label.
